title: Adic smooth base change
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its ring of integers $A=\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Consider a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
e\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
T&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Assume $f$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all four schemes noetherian [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\ell$ invertible on $S$. Use the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], indexed here by $n\geq0$ with $A_n=A/I^{n+1}$ and $I=(\varpi)$; every $A_n$ is finite of order invertible on the four schemes and perfect over $A$. At a corner $W$, the integral coefficient sheaf is $A_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$. Write $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)$ for its full subcategory of derived $I$-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]; completed direct image means the restriction of ordinary $Ru_*$ to complete objects [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange].

Assume $T$ has finite dimension, as required for $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let $K$ belong to that category, and suppose each canonical reduction
$$K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(A_n)_T$$
is in the essential image of $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ under the comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Then the canonical completed adjunction-mate exchange of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]
$$
\alpha_K:Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp}}K
\longrightarrow Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp}}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$
is an isomorphism in $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,A)$.

If $X$ also has finite dimension and there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every $n\geq0$, all four finite-coefficient objects
$$
Rg_{n,*}K_n,\qquad Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}K_n,\qquad Le_n^*K_n,\qquad Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*K_n
$$
have constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$, then both endpoints belong to $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $\alpha_K$ is an isomorphism in that full subcategory. The subscript $n$ on an operation denotes the same scheme morphism with coefficient sheaves $(A_n)_W$.

proof.text: Choose each assumed bounded constructible etale antecedent L_n. Its origin isomorphism and the unit of exact pbcDerivedFunctionRealization identify comparisonUpperStar L_n with the inverse-realization coordinate V_n. Realize V_n by finiteCoefficientRealization and use its canonical derived composition comparison to obtain the bounded constructible finite-coefficient origin hypothesis. Apply the recorded finite pro-etale smooth-base-change theorem with N = Nat.card(A_n), positive because A_n is a finite unital ring, annihilating A_n by the additive group cardinality theorem, and invertible on S by assumption. Reflection by exact finite realization and naturality at its equivalence unit give invertibility of fixed-scalar exchange at V_n. The finite exchange encoding gives invertibility of sbcFiniteExchangeApp at the actual reduction.

proof.text: The two source and two target reduction comparisons from sbcReductionComparisons_isIso are invertible. Substitute them into sbcCompletedOperations_linear_natural_exchange. The right hand side is a composite of isomorphisms by step 1. Cancel the two target comparisons to show that every actual quotient reduction of the completed exchange is invertible.

proof.text: Apply completedReductionEvaluation to the strict quotient tower. Its invertible comparison identifies each derived evaluation of the tower map with exact restriction of the corresponding invertible reduction from step 2. Exact evaluation commutes with homology, and pointwise invertibility of a natural transformation gives invertibility of the tower map. Intrinsic completeness of each endpoint implies TowerComplete by pbcIntrinsicComplete_towerComplete. The completion-unit naturality equation then gives invertibility of the original map by cancellation of both completion units. Reflect through the full-subcategory inclusion.

source.place: Tags 099M and 099N, detection by the strict reduction tower and its canonical completion unit

proof.text: For either endpoint compose the pullback and pushforward reduction isomorphisms to its specified finite output. Exact restriction along the level constant comparison commutes with homology. Transport constructibility and vanishing in the common interval along these isomorphisms. The backward uniform reduction criterion supplies uniform local models and compatible etale origins. Intrinsic completeness is already part of the endpoint object, so both endpoints satisfy the full bounded-constructible-complete predicate. The full-subcategory inclusion reflects the isomorphism of step 3.

split_report.summary: Expanded the finite-reduction proof into eight steps, with general completed adjunction-mate comparison and derived-complete detection, and an explicit constructible-membership argument including normalization-compatible etale witnesses. Reused existing nodes only. STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported landing was on S although both endpoints are on X; corrected to X and made the finite-dimension domain conditions of the existing Dbc notation explicit. Distinguished completed coefficient sheaves from finite constant coefficients. Removed the inapplicable proper-base-change theorem as a proof dependency. Q75 resumed from the repository proof after confirming that the sandbox had no prior item or report. Rechecked every cited statement and the current blueprint, removed obsolete further-quotient discussion from step 2, and made the tensor-balancing cocycle in the compatible-witness argument explicit. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the single blueprint proof paragraph: completed actions and perfect projection formula in steps 1 and 3; finite-level smooth exchange in step 2; identification of the specified completed mate in step 4; inverse-limit/completeness detection in step 5; constructible landing in steps 6-8. The unit sk-rem-rest is a roadmap with no numbered steps, and this node is not its key statement.

tool_uses.why: Provides completeness and direct-image/derived-limit commutation for arbitrary g and h; the smooth unit has no direct-image completion theorem.
Identifies actual reductions of completed pullback and supplies completeness for f and e; these are generic completion formulas, not a smooth-base-change assertion.
Identifies finite reductions of Rg_*K and Rh_*E using perfect quotient coefficients without properness; the unit supplies no projection formula.
Compares finite and completed coefficient operations after exact restriction and reflects isomorphisms; needed to type the reduction argument.
Supplies canonical inverse-image coefficient isomorphisms and commutative quotient squares needed for coefficient restriction along every edge.
Detects an isomorphism between complete objects from invertibility of all actual quotient reductions; no smoothness enters this general tool.
Provides A_X/I^m A_X = (A/I^m)_X to make cohomology comparisons quotient-linear; used only for coefficient bookkeeping in the conditional landing.
Turns a normalized reduction tower with constructible cohomology in one interval into the common local models required by the integral category; no base-change invertibility is asserted.

Lifts the normalizations of the actual reduction towers of the two endpoints to compatible etale-origin witnesses; a generic site-comparison lemma with no smooth-base-change content, and no node of the smooth unit gives it.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q75-9be722708 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item and all 8 steps, the 17 proof-dependency and 12 statement-dependency statements, the blueprint_update texts of the six cited nodes that have one, the proof of lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange, the master, main-20261015 and main-20261017 blueprint texts (identical to each other), and Stacks 099N, 09B1 and 09AL. No SGA source is used and there are no new nodes. (1) The square and exchange morphism match 0EYU and the finite theorem's orientation: α_K is the completed unit-θ-counit mate. The coefficients are the completed sheaf A_W, explicitly not identified with constant A; the finite levels (A_n)_W are the same sheaves as Λ_{W,Proet}. The inherited S→X landing correction is right, since both endpoints are on X. The finite-dimension conditions are exactly what the Dbc notation requires, and |A_n| is a power of ℓ and A_n is perfect, so those assumptions are automatic. The target is not weakened. (2) Steps 1–6 and 8 check out. In step 2 all hypotheses of the finite theorem hold with N=|A_n|. Step 3 only claims comparisons after restriction, which ring-sheaf-change-adjunction (b, d) and profinite-coefficient-inverse-image support. In step 4, the 'finite-level exchange' of the cited mate lemma (its steps 13–16) is the restricted ambient (P_n)-exchange at K_n, which is the same map as δ_n of step 2. Step 5 is the last sentence of levelwise-isomorphism-cones. In step 6 the lift argument for (A_n)-linearity and the hypotheses of normalized-constructible-local-effectivity hold. (3) Long step 7 (2457 characters): the argument is correct, but it hides a lemma that is already a DAG node, lem-weil-pbc-normalized-etale-origin-witnesses (Q92, 2026-10-17, unsplit; its statement gives D^+ membership of the lifted tensors, unique β_{m,n} with the γ/ρ equation, β_{n,n}=1, and the cocycle). That is a C5 duplication and a hidden lemma. FIX: step 7 now cites it, with the origins taken from step 6 and ρ from the adic datum. The four nodes that only step 7 used are removed from proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses, and the witness lemma is added as a tool use. This creates no cycle.
